scope: Four available paired outputs from the 13-case frozen comparison; descriptive assistant review only. Other cases remain unavailable under 20B provider limits. This availability subset is not a full model benchmark or a model-winner claim.

cases.observation: Both provide valid examples. Apply the same conditional-rubric adjudication as in stage 2; neither claims to enumerate all catch-completion requirements.
Both preserve the football-act/sufficient-time alternative and distinguish incompletion before completion from later fumble.

20B says a player can lose control on ground contact only if control was not maintained long enough, incorrectly ruling out a later fumble. 120B uses an overbroad only-if incompletion condition. Both have material explanation/ruling limitations.
20B correctly lists two penalty routes, then wrongly generalizes that accepting any defensive penalty awards new downs. 120B retains the two qualifying routes without that generalization.
